# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

sources.title: Python Release Python 3.13.0
sources.snippet:
# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.

sources.title: Python Release Python 3.13.0
sources.snippet:
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.

sources.title: Python Release Python 3.13.0
sources.snippet:
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

# Python 3.13.0

**发布日期：** 2024年10月7日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的稳定版本

Python 3.13.0 是 Python 编程语言最新的主要版本，与 Python 3.12 相比，它包含了许多新特性和优化。（与上一个候选版本 3.13.0rc3 相比，3.13.0 包含两个小的错误修复以及一些文档和测试的变更。）

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。

# Python 3.13.0rc1

**发布日期：**2024年8月1日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

### 核心开发者：是时候着手撰写文档了

* 你们所有的更改都已正确地记录了吗？

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。

# Python 3.13.0rc1

**发布日期：**2024年8月1日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

### 核心开发者：是时候着手撰写文档了

* 你们所有的更改都已正确地记录了吗？

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

sources.title: Python Release Python 3.13.0
sources.snippet:
# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.

sources.title: Python Release Python 3.13.0
sources.snippet:
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

sources.snippet:
# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.

sources.title: Python Release Python 3.13.0
sources.snippet:
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.

sources.title: When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?
sources.snippet:
### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. When you install a package, you can just download the binary wheel and don’t need to compile it (though wheels are harder to come by if you use [Alpine Linux](/articles/alpine-docker-python/), in which case wheels may or may not be available).

But at least for a short time after 3.13’s release, some packages won’t have wheels for Python 3.13 uploaded yet. This is less of a problem these days compared to older Python releases, as:

* Package maintainers are putting in more and more effort to shorten this window, often releasing updated packages in advance of the Python final release.
* Some packages release binary wheels using the forward-compatible “abi3” format, which means newer Python releases just work with no extra effort.

metadata.title: When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?

sources.title: When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?
sources.snippet:
Of course, there’s always another bug fix release in the future, but given a 12-month window between major releases, lots of new code will get written but not extensively used. Which means Python 3.13.0 can also expect a follow-up 3.13.1 release to deal with the results of real-world usage. And indeed, 3.13.1 came out December 3rd, 2024, with [a very long list of bug fixes](https://docs.python.org/release/3.13.1/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-13-1).

## Things are getting better!

I’ve been updating this article over the years since 3.9, and the situation has gotten significantly better since then. Every release I’ve reduced the caveats, and projects have sped up their iteration cycles so they have support for newer releases even faster.

## Is upgrading worth it?

**Given that it takes work to upgrade—some additional testing, some tweaks to your code—it can be tempting to put off upgrading Python versions indefinitely.** Why worry about incompatibilities, new versions, and what not, when you can just stick with your current version indefinitely?

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# More resources

* [Online Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/), 3.13 Release Schedule
* Report bugs at <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues>.
* [Help fund Python directly](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/python-dev/) (or [via GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/python)), and support [the Python community](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/).

# Python 3.13.0

**发布日期：** 2024年10月7日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的稳定版本

Python 3.13.0 是 Python 编程语言最新的主要版本，与 Python 3.12 相比，它包含了许多新特性和优化。（与上一个候选版本 3.13.0rc3 相比，3.13.0 包含两个小的错误修复以及一些文档和测试的变更。）

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性的*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用了全局解释器锁（GIL），允许多个线程更并发地运行。该构建模式也作为实验性功能在 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中提供。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性的* JIT（即时）编译器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能提升奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)。
* Android 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* 在标准库的多个模块中[移除了许多其他](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis)已弃用的类、函数和方法。
* C API 的[移除项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis)和[弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis)。（在 alpha 1 版本中移除的一些项已在 alpha 2 版本中恢复，因为目前认为这些移除项的破坏性太大。）
* [新的弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations)，其中大部分计划在 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

有关 Python 3.13 变化的更多详情，请参阅[《Python 3.13 的新变化》](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。

# 更多资源

* [在线文档](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0719/), 3.13 发布时间表
* 请在 <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues> 报告错误。
* [直接为 Python 提供资金帮助](https://pythonlang.cn/psf/donations/python-dev/)（或[通过 GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/python)），并支持 [Python 社区](https://pythonlang.cn/psf/donations/)。

[完整更新日志](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/release/3.13.0/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-13-0)

# PEP 719 – Python 3.13 发布时间表

作者:
:   Thomas Wouters

## [摘要](#abstract)

本文档描述了 Python 3.13 的开发和发布时间表。

## [发布经理和团队](#release-manager-and-crew)

* 3.13 发布经理：Thomas Wouters
* Windows 安装程序：Steve Dower
* Mac 安装程序：Ned Deily
* 文档：Julien Palard

## [发布时间表](#release-schedule)

### [3.13.0 发布时间表](#schedule)

注意：以下日期采用 17 个月的开发周期，根据 [PEP 602](../pep-0602/ "PEP 602 – Python 年度发布周期") 的定义，导致功能版本之间有 12 个月的发布节奏。

实际

* 3.13 开发开始：2023年5月22日，星期一
* 3.13.0 alpha 1：2023年10月13日，星期五
* 3.13.0 alpha 2：2023年11月22日，星期三
* 3.13.0 alpha 3：2024年1月17日，星期三

* 3.13.0 alpha 5：2024年3月12日，星期二
* 3.13.0 alpha 6：2024年4月9日，星期二
* 3.13.0 beta 1：2024年5月8日，星期三（此后不再添加新功能。）
* 3.13.0 beta 2：2024年6月5日，星期三
* 3.13.0 beta 3：2024年6月27日，星期四
* 3.13.0 beta 4：2024年7月18日，星期四
* 3.13.0 candidate 1：2024年8月1日，星期四
* 3.13.0 candidate 2：2024年9月6日，星期五
* 3.13.0 candidate 3：2024年10月1日，星期二
* 3.13.0 最终版：2024年10月7日，星期一

### [错误修复版本](#bugfix-releases)

实际

* 3.13.1：2024年12月3日，星期二
* 3.13.2：2025年2月4日，星期二
* 3.13.3：2025年4月8日，星期二
* 3.13.4：2025年6月3日，星期二

预期

* 3.13.10：2025年12月2日，星期二
* 3.13.11：2026年2月3日，星期二
* 3.13.12：2026年4月7日，星期二
* 3.13.13：2026年6月9日，星期二
* 3.13.14：2026年8月4日，星期二

### [仅源码安全修复版本](#source-only-security-fix-releases)

在2029年10月之前，将根据需要不定期提供。

### [3.13 生命周期](#lifespan)

3.13 将在大约24个月内，大约每2个月收到一次错误修复更新。在 3.15.0 最终版发布前后，将发布 3.13 的最终错误修复更新。此后，预计将发布安全更新（仅源代码），直到 3.13.0 最终版发布后的5年，即大约到2029年10月。

# Python 3.13.0rc1

**发布日期：**2024年8月1日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

### 核心开发者：是时候着手撰写文档了

* 你们所有的更改都已正确地记录了吗？
* 它们在[新特性](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)中提及了吗？
* 你是否注意到其他已知更改的文档不足？

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[三级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)，[Android 也即将推出](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* [许多其他废弃的类、函数和方法](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed)已从各种标准库模块中移除。
* C API [移除](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#id10)和[废弃](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#id9)。（Alpha 1 中存在的一些移除在 Alpha 2 中被恢复，因为这些移除在当时被认为干扰性太大。）
* [新的废弃项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated)，其中大多数计划从 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

（嘿，**核心开发者们**，如果你们认为重要的功能没有出现在这个列表中，请[告知 Thomas](mailto:thomas@python.org)。）

有关 Python 3.13 更改的更多详细信息，请参阅[Python 3.13 新特性](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。Python 3.13 的下一个预发布版本将是 3.13.0rc2，**也是最终的发布候选版本**，目前定于2024年9月3日发布。

# 更多资源

* [在线文档](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0719/), 3.13 发布时间表
* 请在 <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues> 报告错误。

[完整更新日志](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/changelog.html#changelog)

# PEP 719 – Python 3.13 Release Schedule

Author:
:   Thomas Wouters

Status:
:   Active

Type:
:   Informational

Topic:
:   [Release](../topic/release/)

Created:
:   26-May-2023

Python-Version:
:   3.13

Table of Contents

* [Abstract](#abstract)
* [Release Manager and Crew](#release-manager-and-crew)
* [Release Schedule](#release-schedule)
  + [3.13.0 schedule](#schedule)
  + [Bugfix releases](#bugfix-releases)
  + [Source-only security fix releases](#source-only-security-fix-releases)
  + [3.13 Lifespan](#lifespan)

## [Abstract](#abstract)

This document describes the development and release schedule for Python 3.13.

## [Release Manager and Crew](#release-manager-and-crew)

* 3.13 Release Manager: Thomas Wouters
* Windows installers: Steve Dower
* Mac installers: Ned Deily
* Documentation: Julien Palard

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# More resources

* [Online Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/), 3.13 Release Schedule
* Report bugs at <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues>.

# Python 3.13.0

**发布日期：** 2024年10月7日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的稳定版本

Python 3.13.0 是 Python 编程语言最新的主要版本，与 Python 3.12 相比，它包含了许多新特性和优化。（与上一个候选版本 3.13.0rc3 相比，3.13.0 包含两个小的错误修复以及一些文档和测试的变更。）

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性的*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用了全局解释器锁（GIL），允许多个线程更并发地运行。该构建模式也作为实验性功能在 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中提供。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性的* JIT（即时）编译器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能提升奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)。
* Android 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* 在标准库的多个模块中[移除了许多其他](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis)已弃用的类、函数和方法。
* C API 的[移除项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis)和[弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis)。（在 alpha 1 版本中移除的一些项已在 alpha 2 版本中恢复，因为目前认为这些移除项的破坏性太大。）
* [新的弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations)，其中大部分计划在 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

有关 Python 3.13 变化的更多详情，请参阅[《Python 3.13 的新变化》](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。

# 更多资源

* [在线文档](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0719/), 3.13 发布时间表

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# More resources

* [Online Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/), 3.13 Release Schedule
* Report bugs at <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues>.
* [Help fund Python directly](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/python-dev/) (or [via GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/python)), and support [the Python community](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/).

candidates.title: When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?
candidates.snippet:
# When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?

by [Itamar Turner-Trauring](mailto:itamar@pythonspeed.com)  
Last updated 05 Dec 2024, originally created 12 Sep 2024

Python 3.13 was released October 7, 2024—but should you switch to it immediately? And if you shouldn’t upgrade just yet, when should you?

Immediately after the release, you probably didn’t want to upgrade just yet. But at this point, upgrading is definitely worth trying, though it may not succeed. To understand why, we need to consider Python packaging, the software development process, and take a look at the history of past releases.

## The problems with a new major Python release

As with many open source projects, Python, Python libraries, and most of the toolchain and packages mentioned in this article are based on volunteer labor. None of this should be read as a complaint towards the people doing the maintenance, they’re doing hugely valuable work, released for free and often done for free, and everything takes time. In addition, because upgrades involve so many different groups, coordination and releases take even more time.

With that in mind, let’s consider the problems with using 3.13 immediately after a release, and in the following months:

### 1. Incompatible packages

In some cases, the code in a library is incompatible with a new Python release. Given many Python packages are maintained by volunteers with limited free time and working independently, it just takes time for updates to percolate through the system.

To give an example, at the time of writing, the same week 3.13 came out:

* Numba didn’t support Python 3.13, because its dependency `llvmlite` didn’t support 3.13 yet.
* Twisted didn’t have a release supporting 3.13. The code had been upgraded to support 3.13, but a release was blocked on e.g. `pywin32` getting a 3.13-compatible release, which only happened October 4th.

Looking again in early December, Twisted supports Python 3.13, and Numba has a pre-release out, so will hopefully support it in the near future.

Some of packages will have releases quickly; some will take longer. Again, not a complaint, just a reality of depending on volunteer efforts for key packages.

### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. When you install a package, you can just download the binary wheel and don’t need to compile it (though wheels are harder to come by if you use [Alpine Linux](/articles/alpine-docker-python/), in which case wheels may or may not be available).

But at least for a short time after 3.13’s release, some packages won’t have wheels for Python 3.13 uploaded yet. This is less of a problem these days compared to older Python releases, as:

* Package maintainers are putting in more and more effort to shorten this window, often releasing updated packages in advance of the Python final release.
* Some packages release binary wheels using the forward-compatible “abi3” format, which means newer Python releases just work with no extra effort.

Nonetheless, there will be packages that won’t have binary wheels yet. Best case, that means installation will take a lot longer as you have to compile the code on installation. Worst case, compilation will fail because you don’t have relevant compile-time dependencies installed.

#### Conda support

If you’re using Conda-Forge, the Python 3.13 rollout happens pretty quickly. A lot of it is automated, one of [the benefits of Conda-Forge over PyPI](/articles/conda-vs-pip/), so as long as the underlying packages already support 3.13, it happens pretty quickly across the whole package repository. Here’s [the tracker for the process](https://conda-forge.org/status/migration/?name=python313), it’s very impressive automation.

### 3. Bugs in Python

Python 3.12.0 was released in October 2023. 3.12.1 was released in December 2023, with [more than 400 bugfixes](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-12-1-final).

Of course, there’s always another bug fix release in the future, but given a 12-month window between major releases, lots of new code will get written but not extensively used. Which means Python 3.13.0 can also expect a follow-up 3.13.1 release to deal with the results of real-world usage. And indeed, 3.13.1 came out December 3rd, 2024, with [a very long list of bug fixes](https://docs.python.org/release/3.13.1/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-13-1).

## Things are getting better!

I’ve been updating this article over the years since 3.9, and the situation has gotten significantly better since then. Every release I’ve reduced the caveats, and projects have sped up their iteration cycles so they have support for newer releases even faster.

## Is upgrading worth it?

**Given that it takes work to upgrade—some additional testing, some tweaks to your code—it can be tempting to put off upgrading Python versions indefinitely.** Why worry about incompatibilities, new versions, and what not, when you can just stick with your current version indefinitely?

The problem is that Python isn’t supported indefinitely, nor do libraries support all Python versions indefinitely; eventually you’ll stop getting security updates and bug fixes. [Python 3.8 ended security updates in October 2024](/articles/stop-using-python-3.8/). 3.9 will be next, dropping security updates in October 2025.

So sooner or later you will have to upgrade. And if you’re running on a 5-year-old version of Python, switching becomes a Big Deal—you’ll often end up dealing with more significant cross-version changes in both Python and in libraries at the same time. Which makes upgrading scary.

**Instead of one massive scary upgrade event every few years, it’s much safer to have a continuous, ongoing process of smaller upgrades.** Whenever a new major Python version comes out, or a new major library version, w

# This is the third release candidate of Python 3.13.0

This release, **3.13.0rc3**, is the final release preview (no really) of 3.13. This release is expected to become the final 3.13.0 release, barring any critical bugs being discovered. The official release of 3.13.0 is now scheduled for Monday, 2024-10-07.

This extra, unplanned release candidate exists because of a couple of last minute issues, primarily a significant performance regression in specific workloads due to the incremental cyclic garbage collector (introduced in the alpha releases). We decided to roll back the garbage collector change in 3.13 (and continuing work in 3.14 to improve it), apply a number of other important bug fixes, and roll out a new release candidate.

There will be **no ABI changes** from this point forward in the 3.13 series (and there haven't been any since the beta releases).

## Call to action

We strongly encourage maintainers of Python projects to prepare their projects for 3.13 compatibilities during this phase, and where necessary publish Python 3.13 wheels on PyPI to be ready for the final release of 3.13.0. As always, report any issues to [the Python bug tracker](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues).

## [Abstract](#abstract)

This document describes the development and release schedule for Python 3.13.

## [Release Manager and Crew](#release-manager-and-crew)

* 3.13 Release Manager: Thomas Wouters
* Windows installers: Steve Dower
* Mac installers: Ned Deily
* Documentation: Julien Palard

## [Release Schedule](#release-schedule)

### [3.13.0 schedule](#schedule)

Note: the dates below use a 17-month development period that results in a 12-month release cadence between feature versions, as defined by [PEP 602](../pep-0602/ "PEP 602 – Annual Release Cycle for Python").

Actual:

* 3.13 development begins: Monday, 2023-05-22
* 3.13.0 alpha 1: Friday, 2023-10-13

### [Source-only security fix releases](#source-only-security-fix-releases)

Provided irregularly on an as-needed basis until October 2029.

### [3.13 Lifespan](#lifespan)

3.13 will receive bugfix updates approximately every 2 months for approximately 24 months. Around the time of the release of 3.15.0 final, the final 3.13 bugfix update will be released. After that, it is expected that security updates (source only) will be released until 5 years after the release of 3.13.0 final, so until approximately October 2029.

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# More resources

* [Online Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/), 3.13 Release Schedule
* Report bugs at <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues>.
* [Help fund Python directly](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/python-dev/) (or [via GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/python)), and support [the Python community](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/).

# Python 3.13.0rc1

**发布日期：**2024年8月1日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

### 核心开发者：是时候着手撰写文档了

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[三级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)，[Android 也即将推出](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* [许多其他废弃的类、函数和方法](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed)已从各种标准库模块中移除。
* C API [移除](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#id10)和[废弃](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#id9)。（Alpha 1 中存在的一些移除在 Alpha 2 中被恢复，因为这些移除在当时被认为干扰性太大。）
* [新的废弃项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated)，其中大多数计划从 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

（嘿，**核心开发者们**，如果你们认为重要的功能没有出现在这个列表中，请[告知 Thomas](mailto:thomas@python.org)。）

有关 Python 3.13 更改的更多详细信息，请参阅[Python 3.13 新特性](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。Python 3.13 的下一个预发布版本将是 3.13.0rc2，**也是最终的发布候选版本**，目前定于2024年9月3日发布。

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# Python 3.13.0rc3

Note: Python 3.13.0rc3 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 1, 2024

# This is the third release candidate of Python 3.13.0

This release, **3.13.0rc3**, is the final release preview (no really) of 3.13. This release is expected to become the final 3.13.0 release, barring any critical bugs being discovered. The official release of 3.13.0 is now scheduled for Monday, 2024-10-07.

This extra, unplanned release candidate exists because of a couple of last minute issues, primarily a significant performance regression in specific workloads due to the incremental cyclic garbage collector (introduced in the alpha releases). We decided to roll back the garbage collector change in 3.13 (and continuing work in 3.14 to improve it), apply a number of other important bug fixes, and roll out a new release candidate.

There will be **no ABI changes** from this point forward in the 3.13 series (and there haven't been any since the beta releases).

## Call to action

We strongly encourage maintainers of Python projects to prepare their projects for 3.13 compatibilities during this phase, and where necessary publish Python 3.13 wheels on PyPI to be ready for the final release of 3.13.0. Any binary wheels built against Python 3.13.0rc1 and later **will work** with future versions of Python 3.13. As always, report any issues to [the Python bug tracker](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues).

Please keep in mind that this is a preview release and while it's as close to the final release as we can get it, its use is **not** recommended for production environments.

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

(Hey, **fellow core developer,** if a feature you find important is missing from this list, [let Thomas know](mailto:thomas@python.org).)

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html). The next release of Python 3.13 will be the official 3.13.0 release, currently scheduled for Monday, 2024-10-07.

# When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?

by [Itamar Turner-Trauring](mailto:itamar@pythonspeed.com)  
Last updated 05 Dec 2024, originally created 12 Sep 2024

Python 3.13 was released October 7, 2024—but should you switch to it immediately? And if you shouldn’t upgrade just yet, when should you?

Immediately after the release, you probably didn’t want to upgrade just yet. But at this point, upgrading is definitely worth trying, though it may not succeed. To understand why, we need to consider Python packaging, the software development process, and take a look at the history of past releases.

## The problems with a new major Python release

As with many open source projects, Python, Python libraries, and most of the toolchain and packages mentioned in this article are based on volunteer labor. None of this should be read as a complaint towards the people doing the maintenance, they’re doing hugely valuable work, released for free and often done for free, and everything takes time. In addition, because upgrades involve so many different groups, coordination and releases take even more time.

With that in mind, let’s consider the problems with using 3.13 immediately after a release, and in the following months:

### 1. Incompatible packages

In some cases, the code in a library is incompatible with a new Python release. Given many Python packages are maintained by volunteers with limited free time and working independently, it just takes time for updates to percolate through the system.

To give an example, at the time of writing, the same week 3.13 came out:

* Numba didn’t support Python 3.13, because its dependency `llvmlite` didn’t support 3.13 yet.
* Twisted didn’t have a release supporting 3.13. The code had been upgraded to support 3.13, but a release was blocked on e.g. `pywin32` getting a 3.13-compatible release, which only happened October 4th.

Looking again in early December, Twisted supports Python 3.13, and Numba has a pre-release out, so will hopefully support it in the near future.

Some of packages will have releases quickly; some will take longer. Again, not a complaint, just a reality of depending on volunteer efforts for key packages.

### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. When you install a package, you can just download the binary wheel and don’t need to compile it (though wheels are harder to come by if you use [Alpine Linux](/articles/alpine-docker-python/), in which case wheels may or may not be available).

But at least for a short time after 3.13’s release, some packages won’t have wheels for Python 3.13 uploaded yet. This is less of a problem these days compared to older Python releases, as:

* Package maintainers are putting in more and more effort to shorten this window, often releasing updated packages in advance of the Python final release.
* Some packages release binary wheels using the forward-compatible “abi3” format, which means newer Python releases just work with no extra effort.

Nonetheless, there will be packages that won’t have binary wheels yet. Best case, that means installation will take a lot longer as you have to compile the code on installation. Worst case, compilation will fail because you don’t have relevant compile-time dependencies installed.

#### Conda support

If you’re using Conda-Forge, the Python 3.13 rollout happens pretty quickly. A lot of it is automated, one of [the benefits of Conda-Forge over PyPI](/articles/conda-vs-pip/), so as long as the underlying packages already support 3.13, it happens pretty quickly across the whole package repository. Here’s [the tracker for the process](https://conda-forge.org/status/migration/?name=python313), it’s very impressive automation.

### 3. Bugs in Python

Python 3.12.0 was released in October 2023. 3.12.1 was released in December 2023, with [more than 400 bugfixes](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-12-1-final).

Of course, there’s always another bug fix release in the future, but given a 12-month window between major releases, lots of new code will get written but not extensively used. Which means Python 3.13.0 can also expect a follow-up 3.13.1 release to deal with the results of real-world usage. And indeed, 3.13.1 came out December 3rd, 2024, with [a very long list of bug fixes](https://docs.python.org/release/3.13.1/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-13-1).

## Things are getting better!

I’ve been updating this article over the years since 3.9, and the situation has gotten significantly better since then. Every release I’ve reduced the caveats, and projects have sped up their iteration cycles so they have support for newer releases even faster.

## Is upgrading worth it?

**Given that it takes work to upgrade—some additional testing, some tweaks to your code—it can be tempting to put off upgrading Python versions indefinitely.** Why worry about incompatibilities, new versions, and what not, when you can just stick with your current version indefinitely?

The problem is that Python isn’t supported indefinitely, nor do libraries support all Python versions indefinitely; eventually you’ll stop getting security updates and bug fixes. [Python 3.8 ended security updates in October 2024](/articles/stop-using-python-3.8/). 3.9 will be next, dropping security updates in October 2025.

So sooner or later you will have to upgrade. And if you’re running on a 5-year-old version of Python, switching becomes a Big Deal—you’ll often end up dealing with more significant cross-version changes in both Python and in libraries at the same time. Which makes upgrading scary.

**Instead of one massive scary upgrade event every few years, it’s much safer to have a continuous, ongoing process of smaller upgrades.** Whenever a new major Python version comes out, or a new major library version, wait a bit, and then switch.

The week Python 3.12 was released, you probably didn’t want to upgrade, but you certainly wanted to be using 3.11. Even if you can’t upgrade to 3.13 yet, you should try to upgrade to Python 3.12 if at all possible.

## When should you switch your application to Python 3.13?

At a minimum, after a major new release you will need to wait until:

1. All your libraries explicitly support the new Python release.
2. All the tools you rely on explicitly support the new Python release.

Now that 3.13.1 has come out, you can both get the bug fixes and most packages will be updated, so it’s worth trying to upgrade. If the dependencies you require are still missing 3.13 support, keep trying again every month or two.
