From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

History of the Python programming language

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Python_logo_1990s.svg/250px-Python_logo_1990s.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Python_logo_1990s.svg)

Old Python logo, 1990s–2006

 [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Python_logo_and_wordmark.svg/250px-Python_logo_and_wordmark.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Python_logo_and_wordmark.svg)

New Python logo, 2006–present

 [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Guido-portrait-2014.jpg/250px-Guido-portrait-2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Guido-portrait-2014.jpg)

Guido van Rossum in 2014

The [programming language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language "Programming language") [Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) "Python (programming language)") was conceived in the late 1980s,[[1]](#cite_note-venners-interview-pt-1-1) and its implementation was started in December 1989[[2]](#cite_note-timeline-of-python-2) by [Guido van Rossum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guido_van_Rossum "Guido van Rossum") at [CWI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrum_Wiskunde_&_Informatica "Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica") in [the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Netherlands "The Netherlands") as a successor to [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_(programming_language) "ABC (programming language)") capable of [exception handling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exception_handling "Exception handling") and interfacing with the [Amoeba operating system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amoeba_(operating_system) "Amoeba (operating system)").[[3]](#cite_note-faq-created-3) Van Rossum was Python's principal author and had a central role in deciding the direction of Python (as reflected in the title given to him by the Python community, [*Benevolent Dictator for Life* (BDFL)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benevolent_dictator_for_life "Benevolent dictator for life")[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)) until stepping down as leader on July 12, 2018.[[6]](#cite_note-6) Python was named after the [BBC TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_TV "BBC TV") show *[Monty Python's Flying Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monty_Python's_Flying_Circus "Monty Python's Flying Circus")*.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

Python 2.0 was released on October 16, 2000, with many major new features, such as [list comprehensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_comprehension "List comprehension"), [cycle-detecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycle_detection "Cycle detection") [garbage collector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garbage_collection_(computer_science) "Garbage collection (computer science)"), [reference counting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reference_counting "Reference counting"), [memory management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_management "Memory management") and support for [Unicode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicode "Unicode"), along with a change to the development process itself, with a shift to a more transparent and community-backed process.[[8]](#cite_note-newin-2.0-8)

Python 3.0, a major, backwards-incompatible release, was released on December 3, 2008[[9]](#cite_note-3.0-release-9) after a long period of testing. Many of its major features were also [backported](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backport "Backport") to the backwards-compatible Python versions 2.6 and 2.7[[10]](#cite_note-pep-3000-10) until support for Python 2 finally ceased at the beginning of 2020. Releases of Python 3 up through 3.12 include the `2to3` utility, which automates the translation of Python 2 code to Python 3.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

As of June 2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit), Python 3.14.6 is the latest stable release. This version currently receives full bug-fix and security updates, while Python 3.13—released in October 2024—will continue to receive bug-fixes until October 2026, and after that will only receive security fixes until its end-of-life in 2029. Python 3.10 is the oldest supported branch of Python (albeit in the 'security support' phase).[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13)

## Early history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early history")]

Van Rossum first published the code (for Python version 0.9.1) to alt.sources in February 1991.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) Several features of the language were already present at this stage, among them [classes with inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inheritance_(object-oriented_programming) "Inheritance (object-oriented programming)"), exception handling, functions, and various core [datatypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datatypes "Datatypes") such as `list`, `dict`, and `str`. The initial release also contained a [module system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Module_system "Module system") borrowed from [Modula-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modula-3 "Modula-3"); Van Rossum describes the module as "one of Python's major programming units".[[1]](#cite_note-venners-interview-pt-1-1) Python's exception model also resembled Modula-3's, with the addition of an `else` clause.[[3]](#cite_note-faq-created-3) In 1994 [comp.lang.python](news://comp.lang.python), the primary [discussion forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discussion_forum "Discussion forum") for Python, was formed.[[1]](#cite_note-venners-interview-pt-1-1)

## Version 1

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Version 1")]

Python reached version 1.0 in January 1994. The major new features included in this release were the functional programming tools `lambda`, `map`, `filter` and `reduce`. Van Rossum stated that "Python acquired lambda, reduce(), filter() and map(), courtesy of a [Lisp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisp_(programming_language) "Lisp (programming language)") hacker who missed them and submitted working [patches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patch_(computing) "Patch (computing)")".[[16]](#cite_note-16)

The last version released while Van Rossum was at CWI was Python 1.2. In 1995, Van Rossum continued his work on Python at the [Corporation for National Research Initiatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporation_for_National_Research_Initiatives "Corporation for National Research Initiatives") (CNRI) in [Reston, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reston,_Virginia "Reston, Virginia") from where he released several versions.

By version 1.4, Python had acquired several new features. Notable among these are the Modula-3 inspired [keyword arguments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyword_argument "Keyword argument") (which are also similar to [Common Lisp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Lisp "Common Lisp")'s keyword arguments) and built-in support for [complex numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number "Complex number"). Also included is a basic form of [data hiding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_hiding "Data hiding") by [name mangling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_mangling "Name mangling"), though this is easily bypassed.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

During Van Rossum's stay at CNRI, he launched the Computer Programming for Everybody (CP4E) initiative, intending to make programming more accessible to more people, with a basic "literacy" in programming languages, similar to the basic English literacy and mathematics skills required by most employers. Python served a central role in this: because of its focus on clean syntax, it was already suitable, and CP4E's goals bore similarities to its predecessor, ABC. The project was funded by [DARPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA "DARPA").[[18]](#cite_note-18) As of 2007[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit), the CP4E project is inactive, and while Python attempts to be easily learnable and not too arcane in its syntax and semantics, outreach to non-programmers is not an active concern.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

### BeOpen

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: BeOpen")]

In 2000, the Python core development team moved to BeOpen.com[[20]](#cite_note-20) to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22) CNRI requested that a version 1.6 be released, summarizing Python's development up to the point at which the development team left CNRI. Consequently, the release schedules for 1.6 and 2.0 had a significant amount of overlap.[[8]](#cite_note-newin-2.0-8) Python 2.0 was the only release from BeOpen.com. After Python 2.0 was released by BeOpen.com, Guido van Rossum and the other PythonLabs developers joined [Digital Creations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zope "Zope").

The Python 1.6 release included a new CNRI license that was substantially longer than the CWI license that had been used for earlier releases. The new license included a clause stating that the license was governed by the [laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law "Law") of the [State of Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Virginia "State of Virginia"). The [Free Software Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Software_Foundation "Free Software Foundation") argued that the choice-of-law clause was incompatible with the [GNU General Public License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_General_Public_License "GNU General Public License"). BeOpen, CNRI and the FSF negotiated a change to Python's [free-software license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-software_license "Free-software license") that would make it GPL-compatible. Python 1.6.1 is essentially the same as Python 1.6, with a few minor bug fixes, and with the new GPL-compatible license.[[23]](#cite_note-lib-history-23)

## Version 2

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Version 2")]

Python 2.0, released October 2000,[[8]](#cite_note-newin-2.0-8) introduced [list comprehensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_comprehension "List comprehension"), a feature borrowed from the [functional programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_programming "Functional programming") languages [SETL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SETL "SETL") and [Haskell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell "Haskell"). Python's syntax for this construct is very similar to Haskell's, apart from Haskell's preference for [punctuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punctuation "Punctuation") characters and Python's preference for alphabetic keywords. Python 2.0 also introduced a garbage collector able to collect reference cycles.[[8]](#cite_note-newin-2.0-8)

Python 2.1 was close to Python 1.6.1, as well as Python 2.0. Its license was renamed [Python Software Foundation License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_Software_Foundation_License "Python Software Foundation License"). All code, documentation and specifications added, from the time of Python 2.1's alpha release on, is owned by the [Python Software Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_Software_Foundation "Python Software Foundation") (PSF), a [nonprofit organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization") formed in 2001, modeled after the [Apache Software Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_Software_Foundation "Apache Software Foundation").[[23]](#cite_note-lib-history-23) The release included a change to the language specification to support nested scopes, like other [statically scoped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static_scoping "Static scoping") languages.[[24]](#cite_note-pep-0227-24) (The feature was turned off by default, and not required, until Python 2.2.)

Python 2.2 was released in December 2001;[[25]](#cite_note-25) a major innovation was the unification of Python's types (types written in [C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_(programming_language) "C (programming language)")) and classes (types written in Python) into one hierarchy. This single unification made Python's object model purely and consistently object oriented.[[26]](#cite_note-26) Also added were [generators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generator_(computer_science) "Generator (computer science)") which were inspired by [Icon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icon_(programming_language) "Icon (programming language)").[[27]](#cite_note-pep-0255-27)

Python 2.5 was released in September 2006[[28]](#cite_note-28) and introduced the `with` statement, which encloses a code block within a context manager (for example, acquiring a [lock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lock_(computer_science) "Lock (computer science)") before the block of code is run and releasing the lock afterwards, or opening a [file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_file "Computer file") and then closing it), allowing [resource acquisition is initialization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resource_acquisition_is_initialization "Resource acquisition is initialization") (RAII)-like behavior and replacing a common try/finally idiom.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

Python 2.6 was released to coincide with Python 3.0, and included some features from that release, as well as a "warnings" mode that highlighted the use of features that were removed in Python 3.0.[[30]](#cite_note-pep-0361-30)[[10]](#cite_note-pep-3000-10) Similarly, Python 2.7 coincided with and included features from Python 3.1,[[31]](#cite_note-31) which was released on June 26, 2009. Parallel 2.x and 3.x releases then ceased, and Python 2.7 was the last release in the 2.x series.[[32]](#cite_note-pep-0404-32) In November 2014, it was announced that Python 2.7 would be supported until 2020, but users were encouraged to move to Python 3 as soon as possible.[[33]](#cite_note-33) Python 2.7 support ended on January 1, 2020, along with [code freeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_freeze "Code freeze") of 2.7 development branch. A final release, 2.7.18, occurred on April 20, 2020, and included fixes for critical bugs and release blockers.[[34]](#cite_note-34) This marked the [end-of-life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End-of-life_product "End-of-life product") of Python 2.[[35]](#cite_note-pep-0373-35)

## Version 3

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Version 3")]

"Python 3" redirects here. For the Israeli missile, see [Python (missile) § Python-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(missile)#Python-3 "Python (missile)").

Python 3.0 (also called "Python 3000" or "Py3K") was released on December 3, 2008.[[9]](#cite_note-3.0-release-9) It was designed to rectify fundamental design flaws in the language – the changes required could not be implemented while retaining full backwards compatibility with the 2.x series, which necessitated a new major version number. The guiding principle of Python 3 was: "reduce feature duplication by removing old ways of doing things".[[36]](#cite_note-36)

Python 3.0 was developed with the same philosophy as in prior versions. However, as Python had accumulated new and redundant ways to program the same task, Python 3.0 had an emphasis on removing duplicative constructs and modules, in keeping with the [Zen of Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zen_of_Python "Zen of Python"): "There should be one— and preferably only one —obvious way to do it".

Nonetheless, Python 3.0 remained a [multi-paradigm language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-paradigm_programming_language "Multi-paradigm programming language"). Coders could still follow [object-oriented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object-oriented_programming "Object-oriented programming"), [structured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structured_programming "Structured programming"), and [functional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_programming "Functional programming") programming paradigms, among others, but within such broad choices, the details were intended to be more obvious in Python 3.0 than they were in Python 2.x.

### Compatibility

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Compatibility")]

Python 3.0 broke backward compatibility, and much Python 2 code does not run unmodified on Python 3.[[37]](#cite_note-37) Python's [dynamic typing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_typing "Dynamic typing") combined with the plans to change the semantics of certain methods of dictionaries, for example, made perfect [mechanical translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source-to-source_compiler "Source-to-source compiler") from Python 2.x to Python 3.0 very difficult. A tool called "`2to3`" does the parts of translation that can be done automatically. At this, `2to3` appeared to be fairly successful, though an early review noted that there were aspects of translation that such a tool would never be able to handle.[[38]](#cite_note-38) Prior to the roll-out of Python 3, projects requiring compatibility with both the 2.x and 3.x series were recommended to have one source (for the 2.x series), and produce releases for the Python 3.x platform using `2to3`. Edits to the Python 3.x code were discouraged for so long as the code needed to run on Python 2.x.[[10]](#cite_note-pep-3000-10) This is no longer recommended; as of 2012 the preferred approach was to create a single code base that can run under both Python 2 and 3 using compatibility modules.[[39]](#cite_note-39)

### Features

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Features")]

Some of the major changes included for Python 3.0 were:

* Changing `print` so that it is a [built-in function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsic_function "Intrinsic function"), not a statement. This made it easier to change a module to use a different print function, as well as making the syntax more regular. In Python 2.6 and 2.7 `print()` is available as a built-in but is masked by the print statement syntax, which can be disabled by entering `from __future__ import print_function` at the top of the file[[40]](#cite_note-pep-3105-40)
* Removal of the Python 2 `input` function, and the renaming of the `raw_input` function to `input`. Python 3's `input` function behaves like Python 2's `raw_input` function, in that the input is always returned as a string rather than being evaluated as an expression
* Moving `reduce` (but not `map` or `filter`) out of the built-in namespace and into `functools` (the rationale being code that uses `reduce` is less readable than code that uses a for loop and accumulator variable)[[41]](#cite_note-41)[[42]](#cite_note-42)
* Adding support for optional function annotations that can be used for [informal type declarations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradual_typing "Gradual typing") or other purposes[[43]](#cite_note-pep-3107-43)
* Unifying the `str` and `unicode` types into `str`, representing text, and introducing a separate immutable `bytes` type; and a mostly corresponding mutable `bytearray` type, both of which represent arrays of [bytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byte "Byte")[[44]](#cite_note-pep-3137-44)
* Removing backward-compatibility features, including old-style classes, string exceptions, and implicit relative imports
* A change in [integer division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integer_division "Integer division") functionality: in Python 2, integer division always returns an integer. For example `5/ 2` is `2`; whereas in Python 3, `5/ 2` is `2.5`. (In both Python 2 – 2.2 onwards – and Python 3, a separate operator exists to provide the old behavior: `5// 2` is `2`)
* Allowing non-ASCII letters to be used in identifiers,[[45]](#cite_note-45) such as in `smörgåsbord`
* Unifying integer types `int` and `long` into one integer type: `int`. Python 2 `int` limits integers between `-2147483648` and `2147483647` inclusive. Any integers outside or inside this range have an `L` or `l` suffix such as `-100000000000000L`, `0l`[[46]](#cite_note-46)

### Subsequent releases

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Subsequent releases")]

Python 3.2 defined a stable [ABI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_Binary_Interface "Application Binary Interface"), allowing extension modules to rely on functions across different Python versions.

Python 3.5 added the typing module, which allows for [type hints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_hint "Type hint") and [function signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_signature "Function signature") annotation. It additionally added the [async/await](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Async/await "Async/await") syntax. Furthermore, `.pyo` files were removed, with `.pyc` files representing both unoptimized and optimized [bytecode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bytecode "Bytecode").

Python 3.6 followed with async [generators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generator_(computer_programming) "Generator (computer programming)") and async comprehensions ([for lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_comprehension "List comprehension") as well as dicts and sets), as well as formatted [string literals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_literal "String literal") (f-strings).[[47]](#cite_note-47)

Python 3.10 introduced [structural pattern matching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_pattern_matching "Structural pattern matching") via match/case statements. Additionally it provided improved error messages which "were inspired by previous work in the PyPy interpreter" and added the `|` [union type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_type "Union type") operator.[[48]](#cite_note-48)

Python 3.11 expanded [exception handling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exception_handling_(programming) "Exception handling (programming)") functionality. Around this version, there has been a focus on making Python faster; 3.11 is claimed to be 10–60% faster than 3.10,[[49]](#cite_note-49) and 3.12 increases by an additional 5%.

Python 3.12 added the new keyword `type` and improved error messages.

Python 3.13 added an experimental [just-in-time (JIT) compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just-in-time_compilation "Just-in-time compilation"), the ability to disable the [global interpreter lock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_interpreter_lock "Global interpreter lock"), a new and improved interactive interpreter ([REPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read–eval–print_loop "Read–eval–print loop")), and an incremental [garbage collector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garbage_collection_(computer_science) "Garbage collection (computer science)").[[50]](#cite_note-50) Starting with Python 3.13, it and later versions receive two years of full support (increased from one and a half years), followed by three years of security support; this is the same total duration of support as previously.

Python 3.14 introduced a new tail-calling interpreter as an opt-in feature, offering 3-5% better performance.[[51]](#cite_note-51)

Python 3.15 will "Make [UTF-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8 "UTF-8") mode default";[[52]](#cite_note-52) This mode is supported in all current Python versions, but it currently must be opted into. UTF-8 is already used by default on [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows") (and other [operating systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system")) for most purposes, but an exception is opening files. Enabling UTF-8 also makes code fully [cross-platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-platform_software "Cross-platform software").

#### Security

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=History_of_Python&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Security")]

Security updates were expedited in 2021 and again twice in 2022. More issues were fixed in 2023 and in September 2024 (for Python versions 3.8.20 through 3.12.6)—all versions (including 2.7)[[53]](#cite_note-53) had been insecure because of issues leading to possible [remote code execution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_code_execution "Remote code execution")[[54]](#cite_note-54) and [web-cache poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_poisoning "Cache poisoning").[[55]](#cite_note-55)

# Python 3.13.0

**发布日期：** 2024年10月7日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的稳定版本

Python 3.13.0 是 Python 编程语言最新的主要版本，与 Python 3.12 相比，它包含了许多新特性和优化。（与上一个候选版本 3.13.0rc3 相比，3.13.0 包含两个小的错误修复以及一些文档和测试的变更。）

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性的*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用了全局解释器锁（GIL），允许多个线程更并发地运行。该构建模式也作为实验性功能在 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中提供。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性的* JIT（即时）编译器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能提升奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)。
* Android 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* 在标准库的多个模块中[移除了许多其他](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis)已弃用的类、函数和方法。
* C API 的[移除项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis)和[弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis)。（在 alpha 1 版本中移除的一些项已在 alpha 2 版本中恢复，因为目前认为这些移除项的破坏性太大。）
* [新的弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations)，其中大部分计划在 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

有关 Python 3.13 变化的更多详情，请参阅[《Python 3.13 的新变化》](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

### [3.13 Lifespan](#lifespan)

3.13 will receive bugfix updates approximately every 2 months for approximately 24 months. Around the time of the release of 3.15.0 final, the final 3.13 bugfix update will be released. After that, it is expected that security updates (source only) will be released until 5 years after the release of 3.13.0 final, so until approximately October 2029.

# Python 3.13.0

**发布日期：** 2024年10月7日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的稳定版本

Python 3.13.0 是 Python 编程语言最新的主要版本，与 Python 3.12 相比，它包含了许多新特性和优化。（与上一个候选版本 3.13.0rc3 相比，3.13.0 包含两个小的错误修复以及一些文档和测试的变更。）

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性的*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用了全局解释器锁（GIL），允许多个线程更并发地运行。该构建模式也作为实验性功能在 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中提供。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性的* JIT（即时）编译器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能提升奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)。
* Android 现在是[第 3 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* 在标准库的多个模块中[移除了许多其他](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis)已弃用的类、函数和方法。
* C API 的[移除项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis)和[弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis)。（在 alpha 1 版本中移除的一些项已在 alpha 2 版本中恢复，因为目前认为这些移除项的破坏性太大。）
* [新的弃用项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations)，其中大部分计划在 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

有关 Python 3.13 变化的更多详情，请参阅[《Python 3.13 的新变化》](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# More resources

* [Online Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/), 3.13 Release Schedule
* Report bugs at <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues>.
* [Help fund Python directly](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/python-dev/) (or [via GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/python)), and support [the Python community](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/).

# Python 3.13.0rc1

**发布日期：**2024年8月1日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

### 核心开发者：是时候着手撰写文档了

* 你们所有的更改都已正确地记录了吗？
* 它们在[新特性](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)中提及了吗？
* 你是否注意到其他已知更改的文档不足？

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。
* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）
* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。
* iOS 现在是[三级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0730/)，[Android 也即将推出](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0738/)。

## 类型提示

* 支持在[类型参数中使用类型默认值](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0696/)。
* 一个新的[类型缩小注解](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0742/)：`typing.TypeIs`。
* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

## 移除和新的弃用项

* [PEP 594（从标准库中移除废弃模块）](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0594/)计划移除许多已弃用的模块：`aifc`、`audioop`、`chunk`、`cgi`、`cgitb`、`crypt`、`imghdr`、`mailcap`、`msilib`、`nis`、`nntplib`、`ossaudiodev`、`pipes`、`sndhdr`、`spwd`、`sunau`、`telnetlib`、`uu`、`xdrlib`、`lib2to3`。
* [许多其他废弃的类、函数和方法](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed)已从各种标准库模块中移除。
* C API [移除](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#id10)和[废弃](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#id9)。（Alpha 1 中存在的一些移除在 Alpha 2 中被恢复，因为这些移除在当时被认为干扰性太大。）
* [新的废弃项](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated)，其中大多数计划从 Python 3.15 或 3.16 中移除。

（嘿，**核心开发者们**，如果你们认为重要的功能没有出现在这个列表中，请[告知 Thomas](mailto:thomas@python.org)。）

有关 Python 3.13 更改的更多详细信息，请参阅[Python 3.13 新特性](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html)。Python 3.13 的下一个预发布版本将是 3.13.0rc2，**也是最终的发布候选版本**，目前定于2024年9月3日发布。

# Python 3.13.0

Note: Python 3.13.0 has been superseded by [Python 3.13.15](/downloads/release/python-31315/).

**Release date:** Oct. 7, 2024

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. The build mode is available as an experimental feature in the Windows and macOS installers as well.
* A [preliminary, *experimental* JIT](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#an-experimental-just-in-time-jit-compiler), providing the ground work for significant performance improvements.
* The `locals()` builtin function (and its C equivalent) now has [well-defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals), which allows debuggers to operate more consistently.
* A modified version of [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) is now included, optional but enabled by default if supported by the platform, and required for the free-threaded build mode.
* Docstrings now have [their leading indentation stripped](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes), reducing memory use and the size of .pyc files. (Most tools handling docstrings already strip leading indentation.)
* The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.
* The minimum supported macOS version was changed from 10.9 to **10.13 (High Sierra)**. Older macOS versions will not be supported going forward.
* WASI is now a [Tier 2 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#tier-2). Emscripten is no longer an [officially supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms) (but [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) continues to support Emscripten).
* iOS is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0730/).
* Android is now a [Tier 3 supported platform](https://peps.python.org/pep-0738/).

## Typing

* Support for [type defaults in type parameters](https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/).
* A [new type narrowing annotation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0742/), `typing.TypeIs`.
* A new annotation for [read-only items in TypeDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0705/).
* A new annotation for [marking deprecations in the type system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0702).

## Removals and new deprecations

* [PEP 594 (Removing dead batteries from the standard library)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/) scheduled removals of many deprecated modules: `aifc`, `audioop`, `chunk`, `cgi`, `cgitb`, `crypt`, `imghdr`, `mailcap`, `msilib`, `nis`, `nntplib`, `ossaudiodev`, `pipes`, `sndhdr`, `spwd`, `sunau`, `telnetlib`, `uu`, `xdrlib`, `lib2to3`.
* [Many other removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-modules-and-apis) of deprecated classes, functions and methods in various standard library modules.
* C API [removals](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#removed-c-apis) and [deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#deprecated-c-apis). (Some removals present in alpha 1 were reverted in alpha 2, as the removals were deemed too disruptive at this time.)
* [New deprecations](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#new-deprecations), most of which are scheduled for removal from Python 3.15 or 3.16.

For more details on the changes to Python 3.13, see [What's new in Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html).

# More resources

* [Online Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.13/)
* [PEP 719](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/), 3.13 Release Schedule
* Report bugs at <https://github.com/python/cpython/issues>.
* [Help fund Python directly](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/python-dev/) (or [via GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/python)), and support [the Python community](https://www.python.org/psf/donations/).

**发布日期：**2024年8月1日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。

* [dbm 模块](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/library/dbm.html)新增了一个 [dbm.sqlite3 后端](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm)，在创建新文件时默认使用该后端。
* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。
* WASI 现在是[第 2 级支持平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#tier-2)。Emscripten 不再是[官方支持的平台](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0011/#no-longer-supported-platforms)（但 [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) 会继续支持 Emscripten）。

# When should you upgrade to Python 3.13?

by [Itamar Turner-Trauring](mailto:itamar@pythonspeed.com)  
Last updated 05 Dec 2024, originally created 12 Sep 2024

Python 3.13 was released October 7, 2024—but should you switch to it immediately? And if you shouldn’t upgrade just yet, when should you?

Immediately after the release, you probably didn’t want to upgrade just yet. But at this point, upgrading is definitely worth trying, though it may not succeed. To understand why, we need to consider Python packaging, the software development process, and take a look at the history of past releases.

## The problems with a new major Python release

As with many open source projects, Python, Python libraries, and most of the toolchain and packages mentioned in this article are based on volunteer labor. None of this should be read as a complaint towards the people doing the maintenance, they’re doing hugely valuable work, released for free and often done for free, and everything takes time. In addition, because upgrades involve so many different groups, coordination and releases take even more time.

### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. # 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. When you install a package, you can just download the binary wheel and don’t need to compile it (though wheels are harder to come by if you use [Alpine Linux](/articles/alpine-docker-python/), in which case wheels may or may not be available).

But at least for a short time after 3.13’s release, some packages won’t have wheels for Python 3.13 uploaded yet. This is less of a problem these days compared to older Python releases, as:

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Python 3.13.0

**发布日期：** 2024年10月7日

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的稳定版本

Python 3.13.0 是 Python 编程语言最新的主要版本，与 Python 3.12 相比，它包含了许多新特性和优化。（与上一个候选版本 3.13.0rc3 相比，3.13.0 包含两个小的错误修复以及一些文档和测试的变更。）

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

# 这是 Python 3.13.0 的第一个发布候选版本。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。

此版本 **3.13.0rc1** 是倒数第二个发布预览版。进入发布候选阶段后，此发布候选版本与最终发布版本之间只允许经过审查的、明确的错误修复代码更改。第二个候选版本（也是最后一个计划的发布预览版）定于2024年9月3日星期二发布，而 3.13.0 的正式发布定于2024年10月1日星期二发布。

从现在起，3.13 系列将**不再进行 ABI 更改**，目标是尽可能减少代码更改。

## 行动号召

我们强烈鼓励第三方 Python 项目的维护者在此阶段准备其项目与 3.13 的兼容性，并在必要时在 PyPI 上发布 Python 3.13 wheel 包，以准备 3.13.0 的最终发布。针对 Python 3.13.0rc1 构建的任何二进制 wheel 包**将与**未来版本的 Python 3.13 兼容。一如既往，请向[Python 错误跟踪器](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues)报告任何问题。

请记住，这是一个预览版本，尽管它与最终版本尽可能接近，但**不**建议将其用于生产环境。

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. * The [dbm module](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/dbm.html) has a new [dbm.sqlite3 backend](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#dbm) that is used by default when creating new files.

### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. When you install a package, you can just download the binary wheel and don’t need to compile it (though wheels are harder to come by if you use [Alpine Linux](/articles/alpine-docker-python/), in which case wheels may or may not be available).

But at least for a short time after 3.13’s release, some packages won’t have wheels for Python 3.13 uploaded yet. This is less of a problem these days compared to older Python releases, as:

* Package maintainers are putting in more and more effort to shorten this window, often releasing updated packages in advance of the Python final release.
* Some packages release binary wheels using the forward-compatible “abi3” format, which means newer Python releases just work with no extra effort.

Of course, there’s always another bug fix release in the future, but given a 12-month window between major releases, lots of new code will get written but not extensively used. Which means Python 3.13.0 can also expect a follow-up 3.13.1 release to deal with the results of real-world usage. And indeed, 3.13.1 came out December 3rd, 2024, with [a very long list of bug fixes](https://docs.python.org/release/3.13.1/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-13-1).

## Things are getting better!

I’ve been updating this article over the years since 3.9, and the situation has gotten significantly better since then. Every release I’ve reduced the caveats, and projects have sped up their iteration cycles so they have support for newer releases even faster.

## Is upgrading worth it?

**Given that it takes work to upgrade—some additional testing, some tweaks to your code—it can be tempting to put off upgrading Python versions indefinitely.** Why worry about incompatibilities, new versions, and what not, when you can just stick with your current version indefinitely?

# 3.13 系列相较于 3.12 的主要新特性

Python 3.13 的一些主要新特性和变化如下：

## 新特性

* 一个基于 [PyPy](https://pypy.pythonlang.cn) 的[全新且改进的交互式解释器](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter)，具有多行编辑和颜色支持，以及带颜色的[异常追溯信息](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages)。
* 一个[*实验性*自由线程构建模式](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#free-threaded-cpython)，它禁用全局解释器锁，允许线程更并发地运行。此构建模式也可作为 Windows 和 macOS 安装程序中的实验性功能使用。
* 一个[初步的、*实验性* JIT](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#experimental-jit-compiler)，为显著的性能改进奠定了基础。
* 内置函数 `locals()`（及其 C 语言等效函数）在[修改其返回的映射时](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#defined-mutation-semantics-for-locals)，现在有了明确定义的语义，这使得调试器可以更一致地运行。
* （循环）垃圾收集器现在是[增量的](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#incremental-garbage-collection)，这意味着在有大量对象的程序中，收集暂停时间会更短。
* 现已包含 [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) 的修改版本，这是一个可选功能，但在平台支持的情况下默认启用，并且是自由线程构建模式所必需的。

* 文档字符串（Docstrings）现在会[去除前导缩进](https://docs.pythonlang.cn/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#other-language-changes)，从而减少了内存使用和 .pyc 文件的大小。（大多数处理文档字符串的工具已经会去除前导缩进。）

* 支持的最低 macOS 版本从 10.9 更改为 **10.13 (High Sierra)**。未来的版本将不再支持更旧的 macOS。

* 一个用于 [TypeDict 中只读项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0705/)的新注解。
* 一个用于[在类型系统中标记弃用项](https://peps.pythonlang.cn/pep-0702)的新注解。

# This is the stable release of Python 3.13.0

Python 3.13.0 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations compared to Python 3.12. (Compared to the last release candidate, 3.13.0rc3, 3.13.0 contains two small bug fixes and some documentation and testing changes.)

# Major new features of the 3.13 series, compared to 3.12

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.13 are:

## New features

* A [new and improved interactive interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#a-better-interactive-interpreter), based on [PyPy](https://pypy.org)'s, featuring multi-line editing and color support, as well as colorized [exception tracebacks](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#improved-error-messages).
* An [*experimental* free-threaded build mode](https://docs.python.org/3.13/whatsnew/3.13.html#whatsnew313-free-threaded-cpython), which disables the Global Interpreter Lock, allowing threads to run more concurrently. ### 2. Missing binary packages

Even if the code is compatible, not all packages can be easily installed on 3.13 yet.

Typically, Python package maintainers upload compiled versions of their packages–known as “wheels”–to PyPI. When you install a package, you can just download the binary wheel and don’t need to compile it (though wheels are harder to come by if you use [Alpine Linux](/articles/alpine-docker-python/), in which case wheels may or may not be available).

But at least for a short time after 3.13’s release, some packages won’t have wheels for Python 3.13 uploaded yet. This is less of a problem these days compared to older Python releases, as:

* Package maintainers are putting in more and more effort to shorten this window, often releasing updated packages in advance of the Python final release.
* Some packages release binary wheels using the forward-compatible “abi3” format, which means newer Python releases just work with no extra effort.

Of course, there’s always another bug fix release in the future, but given a 12-month window between major releases, lots of new code will get written but not extensively used. Which means Python 3.13.0 can also expect a follow-up 3.13.1 release to deal with the results of real-world usage. And indeed, 3.13.1 came out December 3rd, 2024, with [a very long list of bug fixes](https://docs.python.org/release/3.13.1/whatsnew/changelog.html#python-3-13-1).

## Things are getting better!

I’ve been updating this article over the years since 3.9, and the situation has gotten significantly better since then. Every release I’ve reduced the caveats, and projects have sped up their iteration cycles so they have support for newer releases even faster.

## Is upgrading worth it?

**Given that it takes work to upgrade—some additional testing, some tweaks to your code—it can be tempting to put off upgrading Python versions indefinitely.** Why worry about incompatibilities, new versions, and what not, when you can just stick with your current version indefinitely?
